commentary:
Episode 10, titled 'Sorting Hogs,' was a double-elimination night that cemented Sharonda Cox as the dominant strategic force in the game. At the first Tribal Council, Sharonda orchestrated a 7-1-1 vote that sent Maggie Nestor — who had been pressing Devin about his fake idol and was building a threat-eliminating coalition — to the jury in 9th place. Only Maggie and Thien An were left out of the vote, underscoring Sharonda's remarkable reach across multiple alliances: her secret Helicopter Alliance with Devin and Jelly, her OG Savu bond with Carter and Cristian, and her control over Eric. At the second Tribal Council, Sharonda again outmaneuvered the field, flipping the vote onto Carter despite Carter holding an unplayed hidden immunity idol, eliminating him 5-2-1 and sending him to the jury in 8th place with his idol still in his pocket — a catastrophic error that Jeff Probst publicly broke down afterward.

Sharonda remains the clear top-ranked player entering the final seven. She is the only castaway with a foot in every remaining alliance, jury relationships with virtually every eliminated player, and two consecutive Tribal Councils worth of proof that she can bend the vote to her will without anyone fully understanding her role. Devin Way rises to second: his fake idol gambit survived scrutiny and, with Maggie gone, the heat on him has cooled somewhat, and his core Helicopter Alliance with Sharonda and Jelly remains the strongest trio in the game. Jelly holds third — her bold earlier moves earn jury respect, and her tight bond with both Devin and Sharonda gives her multiple paths to the end, though her high profile keeps her a target. Cristian jumps to fourth after winning the second immunity challenge in impressive fashion, displaying both physical and social dexterity, though he was left confused about who actually ran the Carter vote, suggesting Sharonda is a step ahead of him.

Mike Pinsky slots fifth — a two-time individual immunity winner this season who is playing both sides but lacks the deeper alliance infrastructure to make a true run at the title. Thien An Nguyen falls to sixth: she was left out of both votes in this episode, her closest ally Maggie is now gone, and while her competitive fire is evident, she is currently isolated and scrambling. Eric Macksoud rounds out the rankings in seventh — consistently in the middle and hard to read, he has avoided the vote-off spotlight, but his apparent role as Sharonda's instrument rather than an independent operator limits his ceiling and jury narrative heading into the endgame.
